- If sentiment is consistently bullish (≥1.0) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤-1.0) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for mean reversion or sentiment-driven rebound.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), model often overcorrects; reduce forecast by 2–5% in next period to avoid overshoot.
- If model forecast is significantly above true (e.g., >10% over 30d), check sentiment history for recent negative signals — if present, adjust downward by 5–10%.
- If model forecast is consistently below true (e.g., <10% under), sentiment may be overly bearish — adjust upward by 3–7% if sentiment turns positive.
- Model tends to lag in early periods (first 5–7 days of forecast) — if true outcome rises sharply early, model may be too conservative; increase first 3–5 days by 2–5%.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model may misalign with sentiment direction — align forecast slope with sentiment trend direction.
- For 30d forecasts, if true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of price correction), reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
